title: OpenAI warns GPT-6.2 Astra will hit usage limits 40% faster because it fixed a bug
content_md: OpenAI confirmed that it fixed a 'bug' that incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 usage, which means you'll now hit GPT usage limits 40% faster than before. In a post on X, Tibo Sottiaux, who works on Codex and ChatGPT at OpenAI, admitted to a billing mistake that incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage for most users. OpenAI says it has fixed the issue but warned that the same tasks will now consume more of users' allowances. "We've fixed this now, so the same work will use more of your plan's usage allowance," Sottiaux explained. "Comparing to last week, you will reach your limits 40% faster on GPT-6.2 Astra and 25% faster on Sol." However, OpenAI says both models will still offer better usage efficiency than their predecessors, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI says it won't charge users for the usage difference caused by the mistake, but it is offering something in return for the disruption. "As a small token to apologize for the mistake, we'll be adding one banked reset for everyone on Go, Plus, Pro, and Business," Sottiaux said. I can confirm that a new reset has been added to ChatGPT, and it expires a month later. So, if you go to ChatGPT Settings > Usage and click Reset, you can restore your exhausted usage limits. As much as I appreciate OpenAI giving its users a free usage reset, it's important to understand that this isn't equivalent to getting 40% less usage. You're still going to use your tokens much faster, and it's unclear when OpenAI will reduce the cost
